messages.subject: Re: CANOPY question
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jonathan,

Do you have total copy number calls? If you are performing situations, can you generate fractional allele-specific copy numbers? Canopy takes as input fractional allele-specific copy number, the signal of which is mixed with purity and ploidy (we don’t estimate purity and ploidy from the copy number estimate step and defer this to Canopy). Another way is to focus on point mutations only however we don’t think this is the major contribution of Canopy.

Feel free to let me know if you have further questions.

Yuchao

> On Sep 3, 2017, at 3:57 PM, Chang, Jonathan <jonatha...@brown.edu> wrote:
>
> Hi Dr. Jiang,
>
> I hope you are well. My name is Jonathan Chang, and I am currently a student at Brown University studying computational biology. I am sending this e-mail because I would love to run some simulated data through CANOPY; however, I do not have BAM files which are needed to get the allele specific copy number estimations using FALCON or SEQUENZA. I currently have copy number calls. Is there anyway I can still run this data? Thank you!
>
> Best,
> Jonathan Chang

messages.subject: RE: Canopy of problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Most likely you didn’t run MCMC long enough and after your binning and thinning, you are left with no posterior trees. You can either let your sampling run longer or adjust the binning and thinning parameters.

Yuchao

Hi Jonathan,

Sorry for my late reply! See my answer below.

It means the allele-specific copy numbers which are fractions due to cancer heterogeneity. Let’s say in this bulk sample you have 10% normal cells, 40% cancer subclone 1 with homozygous deletion and 50% cancer subclone 2 with heterozygous deletion. Then the major copy is  1*10% + 0*40% + 1 * 50% = 0.6 and the minor copy is 1*10% + 0*40% + 0*50% = 0.1

How to generate data input can be found here https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/blob/master/instruction/SNA_CNA_input.md

Yuchao

> On Sep 4, 2017, at 5:31 AM, 徐孝明 <xuxiaom...@163.com> wrote:
>
> Jang老师您好：
>         我是一名做生物信息的新人，您可以叫我小明。我最近在用您开发的R包：canopy，其中有一些地方一直没弄明白，向您请教：
>         1. 输入数据类型中，CNV分为major和minor。我们平时进行CNV检测得到的应该就是major CNV，那minor CNV是怎么得到的？minor CNV对结果的影响有多大？

Major and minor copy number refers to allele-specific copy number. I think what you were referring to was total copy number, which is the sum of the two. How to generate CNV input can be found here https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/blob/master/instruction/SNA_CNA_input.md

>         2. canopy.BIC()中的参数burnin和thin具体发挥什么功能呢？为什么这两个参数的设置会对R包能否正常运行有影响，您推荐的设置brunin=100，thin=5是如何得来的？最优的参数选择是以什么为评判标准？本批样品所适合的最优参数还能否适用于下批样品的检测（是否具有兼容性）？

Burnin and thinning are for MCMC sampling. The default values are selected so that all posterior trees are from sampling that has converged. There is a pdf with posterior likelihood and acceptance rate generated by default by Canopy. You can refer to the plot to make a choice of the parameters. If you are not familiar with MCMC, it is recommended that you keep all default parameters in the demo code. https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/tree/master/demo_code

>         希望Jang老师能够解答我的一些疑问。期待您的回信
>
> 祝好！
> 徐孝明
